classification.difficultyReason: Model the shooting window as the angle opposite the goal width in an SSS triangle.

content.prompt: A soccer goal is 8 m wide. A player shoots for goal (along the ground) when 20 m from one post and 15 m from the other post. Within what angle (correct to the nearest 0.1 degree) must the shot be made for the player to have a chance of scoring a goal?

spec.description: Small perspective goal at left with red frame and netting. Two blue ground segments converge at an unlabelled shooting point at lower right. Black measurements only; no added vertex names or angle annotation. Perspective proportions follow the source rather than a scale triangle.
spec.mathematics: Goal mouth 8 m; shooting distances 20 m from left post and 15 m from right post. Unknown angle at their common shooting endpoint.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the angle at the player's position.
$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{20^2+15^2-8^2}{2(20)(15)}\\\cos\theta&=\frac{561}{600}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{561}{600}\right)\\\theta&\approx20.8^\circ\end{align*}$$
